summary: Fix conflates 'default_ordering flag' with 'ordering derived from Meta.ordering'; since default_ordering stays True even when the user calls explicit .order_by(), the new guard also suppresses adding explicit order-by columns to GROUP BY, changing aggregation results for that common case instead of narrowly targeting Meta.ordering fallback.

issues.description: self.query.default_ordering is only False when the user explicitly clears ordering via a bare .order_by(); it remains True both for implicit Meta.ordering fallback and for explicit .order_by('field') calls. The new `if not self.query.default_ordering` guard therefore can't distinguish the two cases it needs to distinguish, and ends up skipping the GROUP BY population step in the common case (default_ordering True) even when ordering was explicitly requested by the caller, not derived from Meta.ordering.

Aggregate querysets that call .order_by('some_field') explicitly (default_ordering still True) will no longer get that field added to GROUP BY, silently altering grouping/aggregation semantics for a previously-supported and common pattern — a regression beyond the Meta.ordering scope the issue targets.
